rounds.text: The business demonstrates a powerful operational inflection, highlighted by a quarterly operating margin of 40% in June 2026, representing a massive 20 percentage point expansion over the year-ago quarter [E22]. This momentum is backed by robust fundamental delivery, featuring a net profit growth of 60% year-on-year alongside a strong results score of 89 out of 100 [E49, E55]. Compounded profit growth over the past 5 years sits at a solid 23%, validating the long-term earnings power of the enterprise [E11]. Furthermore, the company maintains a pristine balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and positive free cash flow of Rs 0.17 Cr, where operating cash flow reached 117% of operating profit in March 2026 [E26, E27, E28, E29]. Conceded: [E8], [E34], [E45].

The valuation of Khandelwal Extractions Ltd is severely detached from fundamentals, trading at a demanding P/E of 62.6x and 5.00x book value while offering a dividend yield of 0.00% [E1, E2, E4]. A discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 118 per share against a market price of Rs 184, resulting in a negative margin of safety of -56.0%, with the reverse DCF demanding an aggressive 23.8% earnings growth rate [E34, E35, E36]. Operational quality remains lacklustre, evidenced by a low ROCE of 9.6%, an ROE of 6.9%, and a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of -25% [E6, E7, E8]. Furthermore, working capital days have deteriorated significantly from 14.3 days to 80.4 days, and operating margins have compressed by 15 percentage points in the TTM period compared to three years earlier [E21, E45]. conceded: [E22]

While the bear points to high valuation multiples and DCF outputs [E1, E2, E34], the business is currently demonstrating a powerful operational turnaround that raw static models miss, highlighted by a massive quarterly operating margin expansion of +20 percentage points in June 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E22], robust net profit growth of +60% YoY [E49], and sales surging +33% YoY [E47]. The criticism regarding a lacklustre ROCE of 9.6% [E6] ignores that the sector median ROCE sits closely behind at 10.3% [E59], meaning the company operates largely in line with its peer group's capital efficiency while generating superior recent momentum. Conceded: [E1, E2, E8, E34, E45]. The company's balance sheet remains completely pristine with debt-to-equity at 0.00x and zero borrowings [E29, E30], making concerns about financial leverage entirely unfounded. Finally, operating cash flow for March 2026 reached Rs 0.17 Cr, representing an exceptional 117% conversion rate against operating profit [E26, E28], proving that recent earnings expansion is backed by real cash generation rather than accounting distortions.

Conceded: [E22, E47, E49]. The bull's celebration of recent quarterly margin expansion and top-line jumps ignores that the company's longer-term sales trajectory is severely broken, with a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of -25% and a -4% decline over the trailing twelve months [E8, E9]. Furthermore, while the balance sheet is debt-free [E29, E30] and cash flow conversion looks healthy for one period [E26, E28], working capital conditions have deteriorated significantly as working capital days ballooned from 14.3 days to 80.4 days [E45]. The argument that the company's 9.6% ROCE [E6] aligns with the sector median of 10.3% [E59] merely confirms that the business is a mediocre capital allocator in an unexceptional peer group, masking the poor 10-year median return on equity of -3% [E17]. Finally, paying a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4] despite reported profits [E42] and trading at a steep 62.6 P/E [E1] and 5.00x book value [E2] means shareholders are absorbing massive valuation risk for a micro-cap priced miles above its DCF intrinsic value [E34].
